- The Kubernetes namespace containing the workflow (default: \"argo-workflows\")\n114\t///\n115\t/// # Returns\n116\t///\n117\t/// * `Result<WorkflowPhase>` — The workflow's current phase, or an error if:\n118\t///   - kubectl is not available\n119\t///   - The kubeconfig file does not exist\n120\t///   - The workflow does not exist\n121\t///   - kubectl command fails\n122\t///\n123\t/// # Errors\n124\t///\n125\t/// This function returns an error if:\n126\t/// - The kubectl binary cannot be executed\n127\t/// - The kubeconfig file at `/home/coding/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig` is missing\n128\t/// - The workflow does not exist in the specified namespace\n129\t/// - kubectl returns a non-zero exit code\n130\t/// - kubectl output cannot be parsed\n131\t///\n132\t/// # Examples\n133\t///\n134\t/// ```no_run\n135\t/// use needle::kubectl::get_workflow_phase;\n136\t///\n137\t/// # async fn example() -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n138\t/// // Fetch the phase of a workflow in the default namespace\n139\t/// let phase = get_workflow_phase(\"my-workflow\", Some(\"argo-workflows\"))?;\n140\t/// println!(\"Workflow phase: {:?}\", phase);\n141\t/// # Ok(())\n142\t/// # }\n143\t/// ```\n144\t///\n145\t/// # kubectl command\n146\t///\n147\t/// The function executes:\n148\t///\n149\t/// ```bash\n150\t/// kubectl --kubeconfig=/home/coding/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig \\\n151\t///   get workflow <workflow_name> -n <namespace> \\\n152\t///   -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}'\n153\t/// ```\n154\tpub fn get_workflow_phase(workflow_name: &str, namespace: Option<&str>) -> Result<WorkflowPhase> {\n155\t    // Default to argo-workflows namespace if not specified\n156\t    let ns = namespace.unwrap_or(\"argo-workflows\");\n157\t\n158\t    // Verify kubeconfig exists before running kubectl\n159\t    if !std::path::Path::new(IAD_CI_KUBECONFIG).exists() {\n160\t        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n161\t            \"kubeconfig not found: {} (iad-ci cluster access unavailable)\",\n162\t            IAD_CI_KUBECONFIG\n163\t        ));\n164\t    }\n165\t\n166\t    // Build kubectl command with jsonpath to extract status.phase\n167\t    let output = Command::new(\"kubectl\")\n168\t        .arg(\"--kubeconfig\")\n169\t        .arg(IAD_CI_KUBECONFIG)\n170\t        .arg(\"get\")\n171\t        .arg(\"workflow\")\n172\t        .arg(workflow_name)\n173\t        .arg(\"-n\")\n174\t        .arg(ns)\n175\t        .arg(\"-o\")\n176\t        .arg(\"jsonpath={.status.phase}\")\n177\t        .output()\n178\t        .context(\"failed to execute kubectl command\")?;\n179\t\n180\t    // Check if kubectl command failed\n181\t    if !output.status.success() {\n182\t        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);\n183\t        return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n184\t            \"kubectl get workflow failed for '{}/{}': {}\",\n185\t            ns,\n186\t            workflow_name,\n187\t            stderr\n188\t        ));\n189\t    }\n190\t\n191\t    // Parse phase from kubectl output\n192\t    let phase_str = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n193\t    let phase = WorkflowPhase::from_str(&phase_str);\n194\t\n195\t    Ok(phase)\n196\t}\n197\t\n198\t/// Fetch workflow phase with retry logic.\n199\t///\n200\t/// Wraps [`get_workflow_phase`] with automatic retry on transient failures.\n201\t/// Retries up to [`MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS`] times with exponential backoff.\n202\t///\n203\t/// # Arguments\n204\t///\n205\t/// * `workflow_name` - The name of the workflow to query\n206\t/// * `namespace` - The Kubernetes namespace (default: \"argo-workflows\")\n207\t///\n208\t/// # Returns\n209\t///\n210\t/// * `Result<WorkflowPhase>` — The workflow's current phase, or an error if:\n211\t///   - All retry attempts are exhausted\n212\t///   - The workflow does not exist (handled gracefully - see below)\n213\t///   - kubectl is unavailable\n214\t///\n215\t/// # Behavior\n216\t///\n217\t/// - Retries on kubectl command failures (non-zero exit codes)\n218\t/// - **Does NOT retry** \"workflow not found\" errors — treated as graceful failure\n219\t/// - Uses exponential backoff: 1s, 2s, 4s between retries\n220\t/// - Logs each retry attempt with context\n221\tfn get_workflow_phase_with_retry(\n222\t    workflow_name: &str,\n223\t    namespace: Option<&str>,\n224\t) -> Result<WorkflowPhase> {\n225\t    let ns = namespace.unwrap_or(\"argo-workflows\");\n226\t\n227\t    for attempt in 1..=MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS {\n228\t        match get_workflow_phase(workflow_name, namespace) {\n229\t            Ok(phase) => return Ok(phase),\n230\t            Err(e) => {\n231\t                // Check if this is a \"workflow not found\" error\n232\t                let error_msg = e.to_string().to_lowercase();\n233\t                let is_not_found = error_msg.contains(\"not found\")\n234\t                    || error_msg.contains(\"NotFound\")\n235\t                    || error_msg.contains(\"couldn't find\")\n236\t                    || error_msg.contains(\"no such\");\n237\t\n238\t                if is_not_found {\n239\t                    // Workflow not found — don't retry, treat as graceful failure\n240\t                    warn!(\n241\t                        \"Workflow '{}/{}' not found (attempt {}/{}): {}\",\n242\t                        ns, workflow_name, attempt, MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS, e\n243\t                    );\n244\t                    return Err(e);\n245\t                }\n246\t\n247\t                // Other errors may be transient — retry with backoff\n248\t                if attempt < MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS {\n249\t                    let backoff_secs = 2u64.pow(attempt - 1); // 1, 2, 4...\n250\t                    warn!(\n251\t                        \"kubectl get workflow failed for '{}/{}' (attempt {}/{}): {} - retrying in {}s\",\n252\t                        ns, workflow_name, attempt, MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS, e, backoff_secs\n253\t                    );\n254\t                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(backoff_secs));\n255\t                } else {\n256\t                    // Final attempt failed\n257\t                    warn!(\n258\t                        \"kubectl get workflow failed for '{}/{}' after {} attempts: {}\",\n259\t                        ns, workflow_name, MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS, e\n260\t                    );\n261\t                    return Err(e);\n262\t                }\n263\t            }\n264\t        }\n265\t    }\n266\t\n267\t    // This should be unreachable, but handle it for completeness\n268\t    Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n269\t        \"exhausted {} retry attempts for workflow '{}/{}'\",\n270\t        MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS,\n271\t        ns,\n272\t        workflow_name\n273\t    ))\n274\t}\n275\t\n276\t/// Configuration for workflow status polling.\n277\t///\n278\t/// # Fields\n279\t///\n280\t/// * `interval` - Duration between polls (default: 30 seconds, range: 30-60 seconds)\n281\t/// * `namespace` - Kubernetes namespace (default: \"argo-workflows\")\n282\t#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\n283\tpub struct PollConfig {\n284\t    /// Duration between polling attempts.\n285\t    pub interval: Duration,\n286\t    /// Kubernetes namespace containing the workflow.\n287\t    pub namespace: Option<String>,\n288\t}\n289\t\n290\timpl Default for PollConfig {\n291\t    fn default() -> Self {\n292\t        Self {\n293\t            interval: Duration::from_secs(30),\n294\t            namespace: Some(\"argo-workflows\".to_string()),\n295\t        }\n296\t    }\n297\t}\n298\t\n299\timpl PollConfig {\n300\t    /// Create a new poll config with a custom interval.\n301\t    ///\n302\t    /// # Arguments\n303\t    ///\n304\t    /// * `interval_secs` - Polling interval in seconds (must be between 30 and 60)\n305\t    ///\n306\t    /// # Returns\n307\t    ///\n308\t    /// `Result<PollConfig>` — Returns error if interval is out of range.\n309\t    pub fn with_interval(interval_secs: u64) -> Result<Self> {\n310\t        if !(30..=60).contains(&interval_secs) {\n311\t            return Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n312\t                \"polling interval must be between 30 and 60 seconds, got {}\",\n313\t                interval_secs\n314\t            ));\n315\t        }\n316\t        Ok(Self {\n317\t            interval: Duration::from_secs(interval_secs),\n318\t            ..Default::default()\n319\t        })\n320\t    }\n321\t\n322\t    /// Set a custom namespace.\n323\t    pub fn with_namespace(mut self, namespace: &str) -> Self {\n324\t        self.namespace = Some(namespace.to_string());\n325\t        self\n326\t    }\n327\t}\n328\t\n329\t/// Poll workflow status until a terminal phase is reached.\n330\t///\n331\t/// This function repeatedly calls [`get_workflow_phase_with_retry`] at the configured interval\n332\t/// until the workflow reaches a terminal phase (`Succeeded`, `Failed`, or `Error`).\n333\t/// It logs the current phase on each poll iteration.\n334\t///\n335\t/// # Arguments\n336\t///\n337\t/// * `workflow_name` - The name of the workflow to poll\n338\t/// * `config` - Poll configuration (interval, namespace)\n339\t///\n340\t/// # Returns\n341\t///\n342\t/// * `Result<WorkflowPhase>` — The final terminal phase, or an error if:\n343\t///   - kubectl is not available\n344\t///   - The kubeconfig file does not exist\n345\t///   - kubectl commands fail consistently (after retries)\n346\t///   - Workflow-not-found errors exceed [`MAX_FAILED_POLLS`]\n347\t///   - Polling is interrupted\n348\t///\n349\t/// # Errors\n350\t///\n351\t/// This function returns an error if:\n352\t/// - The kubectl binary cannot be executed\n353\t/// - The kubeconfig file is missing\n354\t/// - All kubectl retry attempts are exhausted\n355\t/// - Consecutive poll failures exceed [`MAX_FAILED_POLLS`]\n356\t/// - The polling interval is invalid (via `PollConfig::with_interval`)\n357\t///\n358\t/// # Behavior\n359\t///\n360\t/// - Sleeps for the configured interval between polls\n361\t/// - Logs each poll attempt with the current phase\n362\t/// - Continues polling until a terminal phase is reached\n363\t/// - Treats unknown phases as non-terminal (continues polling)\n364\t/// - **Implements max retry limit:** gives up after [`MAX_FAILED_POLLS`] consecutive failures\n365\t/// - **Handles workflow-not-found gracefully:** logs error without crashing\n366\t///\n367\t/// # Examples\n368\t///\n369\t/// ```no_run\n370\t/// use needle::kubectl::{poll_workflow_status, PollConfig};\n371\t/// # async fn example() -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n372\t/// // Poll with default 30-second interval\n373\t/// let config = PollConfig::default();\n374\t/// let final_phase = poll_workflow_status(\"my-workflow\", &config)?;\n375\t/// println!(\"Workflow completed with phase: {:?}\", final_phase);\n376\t/// # Ok(())\n377\t/// # }\n378\t/// ```\n379\t///\n380\t/// ```no_run\n381\t/// use needle::kubectl::{poll_workflow_status, PollConfig};\n382\t/// # async fn example() -> anyhow::Result<()> {\n383\t/// // Poll with custom 45-second interval in a specific namespace\n384\t/// let config = PollConfig::with_interval(45)?.with_namespace(\"my-namespace\");\n385\t/// let final_phase = poll_workflow_status(\"my-workflow\", &config)?;\n386\t/// println!(\"Workflow completed with phase: {:?}\", final_phase);\n387\t/// # Ok(())\n388\t/// # }\n389\t/// ```\n390\tpub fn poll_workflow_status(workflow_name: &str, config: &PollConfig) -> Result<WorkflowPhase> {\n391\t    let ns = config.namespace.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"argo-workflows\");\n392\t\n393\t    let start_time = Instant::now();\n394\t    let mut consecutive_failures = 0u32;\n395\t\n396\t    info!(\n397\t        \"Starting workflow status poll for '{}/{}' with {}s interval (max failures: {})\",\n398\t        ns,\n399\t        workflow_name,\n400\t        config.interval.as_secs(),\n401\t        MAX_FAILED_POLLS\n402\t    );\n403\t\n404\t    loop {\n405\t        // Fetch current phase with retry logic\n406\t        match get_workflow_phase_with_retry(workflow_name, Some(ns)) {\n407\t            Ok(phase) => {\n408\t                // Reset failure counter on successful fetch\n409\t                consecutive_failures = 0;\n410\t\n411\t                // Log current phase\n412\t                debug!(\n413\t                    \"Workflow '{}/{}' current phase: {:?}\",\n414\t                    ns, workflow_name, phase\n415\t                );\n416\t\n417\t                // Check if terminal\n418\t                if phase.is_terminal() {\n419\t                    let end_time = start_time.elapsed();\n420\t\n421\t                    // Format duration in human-readable format\n422\t                    let duration_str = format_duration(end_time);\n423\t\n424\t                    info!(\n425\t                        \"Workflow '{}/{}' reached terminal phase: {:?} after {}\",\n426\t                        ns, workflow_name, phase, duration_str\n427\t                    );\n428\t\n429\t                    return Ok(phase);\n430\t                }\n431\t\n432\t                // Sleep before next poll\n433\t                debug!(\n434\t                    \"Workflow '{}/{}' still running, sleeping for {}s\",\n435\t                    ns,\n436\t                    workflow_name,\n437\t                    config.interval.as_secs()\n438\t                );\n439\t                std::thread::sleep(config.interval);\n440\t            }\n441\t            Err(e) => {\n442\t                consecutive_failures += 1;\n443\t\n444\t                // Check if workflow was not found (graceful failure)\n445\t                let error_msg = e.to_string().to_lowercase();\n446\t                let is_not_found = error_msg.contains(\"not found\")\n447\t                    || error_msg.contains(\"NotFound\")\n448\t                    || error_msg.contains(\"couldn't find\");\n449\t\n450\t                if is_not_found {\n451\t                    warn!(\n452\t                        \"Workflow '{}/{}' not found (failure {}/{}): {}. This may indicate the workflow \\\n453\t                         hasn't been created yet or was deleted. Giving up.\",\n454\t                        ns, workflow_name, consecutive_failures, MAX_FAILED_POLLS, e\n455\t                    );\n456\t                    return Err(e.context(format!(\n457\t                        \"workflow '{}/{}' not found after polling\",\n458\t                        ns, workflow_name\n459\t                    )));\n460\t                }\n461\t\n462\t                // Check if we've exceeded max retry limit\n463\t                if consecutive_failures >= MAX_FAILED_POLLS {\n464\t                    let total_time = start_time.elapsed();\n465\t                    let duration_str = format_duration(total_time);\n466\t\n467\t                    warn!(\n468\t                        \"Workflow '{}/{}' polling failed {} consecutive times over {}: {}. Giving up.\",\n469\t                        ns, workflow_name, consecutive_failures, duration_str, e\n470\t                    );\n471\t                    return Err(e.context(format!(\n472\t                        \"exceeded max consecutive failures ({}) polling workflow '{}/{}'\",\n473\t                        MAX_FAILED_POLLS, ns, workflow_name\n474\t                    )));\n475\t                }\n476\t\n477\t                // Log warning but continue polling\n478\t                warn!(\n479\t                    \"Workflow '{}/{}' poll failed (failure {}/{}): {}. Retrying in {}s...\",\n480\t                    ns,\n481\t                    workflow_name,\n482\t                    consecutive_failures,\n483\t                    MAX_FAILED_POLLS,\n484\t                    e,\n485\t                    config.interval.as_secs()\n486\t                );\n487\t\n488\t                // Sleep before retry\n489\t                std::thread::sleep(config.interval);\n490\t            }\n491\t        }\n492\t    }\n493\t}\n494\t#[cfg(test)]\n495\tmod tests {\n496\t    use super::*;\n497\t\n498\t    #[test]\n499\t    fn The duration to format\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// A string in the format \"Xm Ys\" where X is minutes and Y is seconds.\n/// For durations less than 1 minute, returns only seconds.\nfn format_duration(duration: Duration) -> String {\n    let total_secs = duration.as_secs();\n    let minutes = total_secs / 60;\n    let seconds = total_secs % 60;\n\n    if minutes > 0 {\n        format!(\"{}m {}s\", minutes, seconds)\n    } else {\n        format!(\"{}s\", seconds)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Represents the phase of an Argo Workflow.\n///\n/// # Variants\n///\n/// * `Running` — Workflow is currently executing\n/// * `Succeeded` — Workflow completed successfully\n/// * `Failed` — Workflow failed with an error\n/// * `Error` — Workflow encountered a system error\n/// * `Pending` — Workflow has not yet started\n/// * `Unknown` — Unable to determine workflow phase\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum WorkflowPhase {\n    Running,\n    Succeeded,\n    Failed,\n    Error,\n    Pending,\n    Unknown(String),\n}\n\nimpl WorkflowPhase {\n    /// Parse a workflow phase string into a [`WorkflowPhase`] enum.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `phase` - .output()\n        .context(\"failed to execute kubectl command\")?;\n\n    // Check if kubectl command failed\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        let stderr = Ok(phase)\n}\n\n/// Fetch workflow phase with retry logic.\n///\n/// Wraps [`get_workflow_phase`] with automatic retry on transient failures.\n/// Retries up to [`MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS`] times with unreachable, but handle it for completeness\n    Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n        \"exhausted {} retry attempts for workflow '{}/{}'\",\n        MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS,\n        ns,\n        workflow_name\n    ))\n}\n\n/// Configuration for workflow status polling.\n///\n/// # Fields\n///\n/// * `interval` - Duration between polls (default: 30 seconds, range: 30-60 seconds)\n/// * `namespace` - Kubernetes and 60 seconds, got {}\",\n                interval_secs\n            ));\n        }\n        Ok(Self {\n            interval: Duration::from_secs(interval_secs),\n            ..Default::default()\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Set a custom namespace.\n    pub fn with_namespace(mut self, namespace: &str) -> Self {\n        self.namespace = Some(namespace.to_string());\n        self\n    }\n}\n\n/// phase (`Succeeded`, `Failed`, or `Error`).\n/// It logs the current phase on each poll iteration.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `workflow_name` - The name of the workflow to poll\n/// * `config` - consecutive_failures = 0;\n\n                // Log current phase\n                debug!(\n                    \"Workflow '{}/{}' current phase: {:?}\",\n                    ns, workflow_name, next poll\n                debug!(\n                    \"Workflow '{}/{}' still running, sleeping for {}s\",\n                    ns,\n                    workflow_name,\n                    config.interval.as_secs()\n                );\n                std::thread::sleep(config.interval);\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                consecutive_failures += 1;\n\n                // Check if workflow was not found (graceful failure)\n                let error_msg = e.to_string().to_lowercase();\n                let is_not_found = error_msg.contains(\"not found\")\n                    || error_msg.contains(\"NotFound\")\n                    || error_msg.contains(\"couldn't find\");\n\n                if is_not_found {\n                    warn!(\n                        \"Workflow '{}/{}' not found (failure {}/{}): {}. Retrying in {}s...\",\n                    ns,\n                    workflow_name,\n                    consecutive_failures,\n                    MAX_FAILED_POLLS,\n                    e,\n                    config.interval.as_secs()\n                );\n\n                // Sleep before retry\n                std::thread::sleep(config.interval);\n            }\n        }\n Start heartbeat emitter\n\n**Transitions:**\n| Condition | Next State |\n|-----------|-----------|\n| Config loaded, bead store healthy | SELECTING |\n| Config invalid | ERRORED |\n| Bead store unreachable | ERRORED (after retry with backoff) |\n\n### SELECTING\n\n**Entry:** Worker is ready for next bead. This is the strand waterfall entry point.\n\n**Actions:**\n1. Emit heartbeat\n2. Evaluate strands in sequence\n3. First strand that yields a candidate bead wins\n\n**Transitions:**\n| Condition | Next State |\n|-----------|-----------|\n| Candidate bead found | CLAIMING |\n| All strands exhausted | EXHAUSTED |\n| Shutdown signal received | STOPPED |\n\n### CLAIMING\n\n**Entry:** A candidate bead has been selected.\n\n**Actions:**\n1. Acquire workspace claim lock (flock, per-workspace)\n2. Verify bead is still claimable (`br show --json`, check status + assignee)\n3. Attempt atomic claim: `br update <id> --claim --actor <worker-id>`\n4. Release workspace claim lock\n5. Emit `bead.claim.attempted` telemetry\n\n**Transitions:**\n| Condition | Exit Code | Next State |\n|-----------|-----------|-----------|\n| Claim succeeded | 0 | BUILDING |\n| Race lost (already claimed) | 4 | RETRYING |\n| Bead no longer claimable (closed, deferred) | 1 | SELECTING |\n| Bead store error | >0 | SELECTING (after backoff) |\n| Max retries exceeded | — | SELECTING (exclude this bead, reset retry counter) |\n\n### RETRYING\n\n**Entry:** A claim attempt failed due to race condition.\n\n**Actions:**\n1. Increment retry counter for this selection cycle\n2. Add failed bead ID to exclusion set\n3. Emit `bead.claim.race_lost` telemetry\n\n**Transitions:**\n| Condition | Next State |\n|-----------|-----------|\n| Retry count < max_retries (default: 5) | CLAIMING (with next candidate from same strand) |\n| Retry count >= max_retries | SELECTING (reset, move to next strand) |\n\n### BUILDING\n\n**Entry:** Bead is claimed by this worker.\n\n**Actions:**\n1. Read full bead context: title, body, dependencies, labels, workspace path\n2. Read workspace context: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .beads/config.yaml\n3. Construct prompt from template (deterministic: same bead → same prompt)\n4. Include bead ID and `br close <id>` instruction in prompt\n5. Emit `prompt.built` telemetry (bead ID, prompt hash, token estimate)\n\n**Transitions:**\n| Condition | Next State |\n|-----------|-----------|\n| Prompt built successfully | DISPATCHING |\n| Bead context unreadable | HANDLING (outcome: failure, release bead) |\n\n### DISPATCHING\n\n**Entry:** Prompt is ready.\n\n**Actions:**\n1. Load agent adapter configuration (YAML)\n2. Resolve invoke template with prompt, workspace path, environment\n3. Start agent process via rendered command\n4. Record process PID, start time\n5. Emit `agent.dispatched` telemetry (agent name, model, workspace)\n\n**Transitions:**\n| Condition | Next State |\n|-----------|-----------|\n| Agent process started | EXECUTING |\n| Agent binary not found | HANDLING (outcome: failure, release bead) |\n| Adapter config invalid | HANDLING (outcome: failure, release bead) |\n\n### EXECUTING\n\n**Entry:** Agent process is running.\n\n**Actions:**\n1. Wait for agent process to exit\n2. Capture stdout, stderr, exit code\n3. Monitor execution timeout\n4. Continue emitting heartbeats while waiting\n5. Emit `agent.executing` heartbeat telemetry periodically\n\n**Transitions:**\n| Condition | Exit Code | Next State |\n|-----------|-----------|-----------|\n| Agent exited normally | any | HANDLING |\n| Execution timeout exceeded | — | Kill process → HANDLING (outcome: timeout) |\n| Shutdown signal received | — | Kill process → HANDLING (outcome: interrupted) |\n\n### HANDLING\n\n**Entry:** Agent has exited (or was killed). This is where outcome routing happens.\n\n**Actions:**\n1. Classify outcome by exit code\n2. Execute the handler for that outcome class\n3. Re-read the bead after the agent process has terminated\n4. If the bead is still `in_progress` and is still assigned to this dispatching\n   worker, invoke the dedicated `resolve` prompt to determine the attempt's\n   semantic outcome\n5. Apply and verify the resulting bead transition\n6. Emit `bead.outcome` telemetry\n\n**Outcome Table:**\n\n| Outcome | Exit Code | Handler | Bead Action |\n|---------|-----------|---------|-------------|\n| **Success** | 0 | Verify bead state. If it remains claimed by this worker, run Resolve. | Closed, released, blocked, or split |\n| **Failure** | 1 | Evaluate for mitosis (see Mitosis section). If splittable, split and block parent. If not, release bead (`br update --status open --unassign`). Increment failure count via label. | Split or released |\n| **Timeout** | 124 | Release bead. Add `deferred` label. | Released + deferred |\n| **Crash** | >128 (signal) | Release bead. Create alert bead in workspace. | Released + alert |\n| **Race Lost** | 4 | (Handled at CLAIMING, should not reach here) | N/A |\n| **Interrupted** | — | Release bead. Clean shutdown. | Released |\n| **Agent Not Found** | 127 | Release bead. Emit error. Do not retry (config issue). | Released |\n| **Build Failure** | — | Release bead. Emit error. | Released |\n\n**Agent-owned closure remains the normal path:** the Pluck agent is instructed\nto close the bead itself. Resolve is an exception-recovery path and runs only\nwhen the agent process has ended while the bead remains `in_progress` and\nassigned to the same worker. It is not invoked for beads the agent already\nclosed, released, or blocked.\n\n**Post-dispatch invariant:** once the dispatched agent process and any Resolve\npass have ended, that dispatch must not leave its bead `in_progress`. A Resolve\nfailure, timeout, invalid response, or failed state mutation falls back to a\nbest-effort release with an explicit `resolution_failed` reason. Ownership is\nchecked again before every mutation so a stale dispatch cannot alter a bead\nthat has since changed hands.\n\n**Resolve decisions:**\n\n| Decision | NEEDLE action |\n|----------|---------------|\n| `complete` | Run configured gates and shipped-work verification; close only if they pass, otherwise release as retryable |\n| `retry` | Record a concise attempt result and retry guidance, increment the failure count, and release with normal retry/backoff policy |\n| `blocked` | Record the concrete external prerequisite and move the bead to the backend's blocked state |\n| `split` | Send the structured child proposal through Mitosis validation/deduplication and apply the parent/child dependency policy |\n\nResolve is advisory: NEEDLE owns validation and all bead mutations. The\nresolver must not edit files, commit, push, or mutate bead state.\n\n**Transitions:**\n| Condition | Next State |\n|-----------|-----------|\n| Outcome processed | LOGGING |\n\n### LOGGING\n\n**Entry:** Outcome has been handled.\n\n**Actions:**\n1. Record effort: elapsed time, exit code, token count (if extractable), estimated cost\n2. Emit `bead.completed` or `bead.released` telemetry\n3. Update worker state registry (beads processed, current streak)\n4. Reset retry counter and exclusion set\n\n**Transitions:**\n| Condition | Next State |\n|-----------|-----------|\n| Logging complete | SELECTING |\n\n### EXHAUSTED\n\n**Entry:** All strands returned no work.\n\n**Actions:**\n1. Emit `worker.exhausted` telemetry\n2. If `idle_timeout` configured, start countdown\n3. If `idle_action` is `wait`, sleep with exponential backoff (max 60s)\n4. If `idle_action` is `exit`, terminate\n\n**Transitions:**\n| Condition | Next State |\n|-----------|-----------|\n| Backoff expired, retry strands | SELECTING |\n| Idle timeout exceeded | STOPPED |\n| Shutdown signal received | STOPPED |\n\n### STOPPED\n\n**Entry:** Graceful shutdown.\n\n**Actions:**\n1. Release any claimed bead\n2. Deregister from worker state registry\n3. Stop heartbeat emitter\n4. Emit `worker.stopped` telemetry\n5. Exit process\n\n**Transitions:** None (terminal).\n\n### ERRORED\n\n**Entry:** Unrecoverable error.\n\n**Actions:**\n1. Release any claimed bead (best-effort)\n2. Emit `worker.errored` telemetry with error details\n3. Deregister from worker state registry (best-effort)\n4. Exit process with non-zero code\n\n**Transitions:** None (terminal).\n\n## Error Model\n\nErrors are classified into three tiers:\n\n### Tier 1: Transient (retry)\n\nTemporary failures that resolve on their own. The worker retries with backoff.\n\n- Bead store temporarily unreachable\n- Claim race lost\n- Lock contention timeout\n- Agent timeout (may succeed on re-dispatch)\n\n### Tier 2: Bead-scoped (release and continue)\n\nFailures specific to one bead. Release it and move on.\n\n- Agent exited with failure\n- Prompt build failed (bead context unreadable)\n- Agent binary missing\n\n### Tier 3: Worker-scoped (exit)\n\nFailures that affect the worker's ability to function. Exit and let the fleet manager handle it.\n\n- Configuration invalid\n- Bead store persistently unreachable\n- Filesystem full\n- Heartbeat file unwritable\n\n## Invariants\n\nThese must hold at all times. Violation of any invariant is a bug.\n\n1. **A worker holds at most one claimed bead.** There is no pipelining or parallel execution within a single worker.\n\n2. **A claimed bead is always released.** Every path through HANDLING releases the bead unless the agent closed it. There is no path where a bead remains claimed after the worker moves to SELECTING.\n\n3. **Heartbeat is continuous.** From BOOTING to STOPPED/ERRORED, the worker emits heartbeats. A gap in heartbeats means the worker is stuck or dead.\n\n4. **Telemetry is emitted for every state transition.** Silent transitions do not exist.\n\n5. **The exclusion set is bounded.** It is cleared on every transition to SELECTING. It cannot grow unboundedly within a selection cycle because max_retries is finite.\n\n6. **Shutdown is always graceful when possible.** SIGTERM triggers STOPPED, not ERRORED. Only SIGKILL causes ungraceful termination, and heartbeat TTL handles that case.\n\n---\n\n# Architecture\n\n## Module Boundaries\n\nNEEDLE is organized into crates (Rust) or packages (Go) with strict dependency rules. No circular dependencies. Each module has a single responsibility.\n\n```\nneedle (binary)\n├── cli/              CLI parsing, session management\n├── worker/           Worker loop, state machine\n├── strand/           Strand waterfall evaluation\n│   ├── pluck.rs      Primary bead selection\n│   ├── mend.rs       Stale claim cleanup, dependency repair\n│   ├── explore.rs    Multi-workspace discovery\n│   ├── weave.rs      Gap analysis, bead creation\n│   ├── unravel.rs    Alternative proposals for HUMAN beads\n│   ├── pulse.rs      Codebase health scans\n│   ├── reflect.rs    Learning consolidation\n│   ├── splice.rs     Worker failure documentation\n│   └── knot.rs       Exhaustion alerting\n├── claim/            Atomic claiming, lock management\n├── prompt/           Prompt construction from bead context\n├── dispatch/         Agent adapter loading, process execution\n├── outcome/          Exit code classification, outcome handlers\n├── commit_hook.rs    Bead-Id trailer injection for git commits\n├── telemetry/        Structured event emission, sinks\n│   └── otlp.rs       OpenTelemetry exporter\n├── health/           Heartbeat, stuck detection, peer monitoring\n├── config/           Hierarchical configuration loading\n├── bead_store/       Abstract bead backend interface\n├── types/            Shared types, error definitions\n├── learning/         Retrospective extraction, learnings management\n├── skill/            Skill library, retrieval, promotion\n├── trace/            Trace capture, storage, retention\n├── transcript/       Session JSONL parsing, action-outcome extraction\n├── drift/            Session similarity, clustering, divergence detection\n├── decision/         Decision point detection, ADR management\n├── placement/        CLAUDE.md lowest-common-ancestor resolution\n├── stats/            Aggregation engine, A/B comparison\n├── supervisor/       Fleet supervisor daemon (auto-scale)\n├── canary/           Release channel promotion, canary tests\n├── upgrade/          Self-update, hot-reload, rollback\n├── registry/         Worker state registry\n├── rate_limit/       Provider/model concurrency and rate limiting\n├── sanitize/         Trace sanitization (gitleaks)\n├── validation/       Pluggable pre-closure validation gates\n├── peer/             Peer monitoring and stale detection\n├── mitosis/          Child-aware bead splitting\n├── span/             W3C trace context utilities\n├── cost/             Token extraction, pricing, cost tracking\n├── agent_event.rs    Agent event telemetry utilities\n├── claude_md_placement.rs  CLAUDE.md placement logic\n└── routing.rs        Model-based adapter routing\n```\n\n### Dependency Graph\n\n```\ncli ──► worker ──► strand ──► bead_store\n prompt ──► bead_store, skill, learning\n                │\n                ├──► dispatch ──► routing\n                │\n                ├──► outcome ──► bead_store, mitosis\n                │\n ├──► config ──► types\n                │\n                ├──► canary ──► worker, upgrade\n                │\n                ├──► upgrade ──► registry, health\n                │\n                ├──► modules)\n```\n\n**Rule:** Arrows point from dependent to dependency. No module depends on `cli` or `worker` except through the binary entry point. `telemetry`, `config`, and `types` are leaf dependencies available to all modules.\n\n## Data Flow\n\n### Primary Loop\n\n```\nbead_store ──[candidates]──► strand ──[bead_id]──► claim ──[claimed_bead]──►\nprompt ──[prompt_string]──► dispatch ──[process]──► worker(wait) ──►\noutcome ──[result]──► bead_store + telemetry\n```\n\n### Telemetry Flow\n\n```\n                    ┌─────────────────────────┐\n                    │    Telemetry Collector   │\n                    └────────────┬────────────┘\n                                 │\n              ┌──────────────────┼──────────────────┐\n              ▼                  ▼                   ▼\n        ┌──────────┐     ┌────────────┐      ┌──────────┐\n        │ File Sink│     │ Stdout Sink│      │ Hook Sink│\n        │ (JSONL)  │     │ (human)    │      │ (webhook)│\n        └──────────┘     └────────────┘      └──────────┘\n```\n\n### Configuration Flow\n\n```\n  CLI args ──► env vars ──► workspace .needle.yaml ──► global ~/.needle/config.yaml ──► defaults\n  (highest)                                                                              (lowest)\n```\n\n## Module Specifications\n\n### bead_store\n\nAbstract interface to any bead backend.
